title: Claim the R&D tax credit
summary: File for the federal research credit (Form 6765): scope the qualified research expenses, run the study, attach the form to the return, and elect the payroll-tax offset (Form 8974) so the credit pays out against payroll — worth up to $500k a year for pre-revenue startups.

parts.title: Confirm eligibility and pick a study provider
parts.guidance: Describe the projects, research activities, entity structure, tax year and prior credit claims for the tax adviser’s initial assessment. Compare study providers on methodology, substantiation, review responsibility and fees. Identify eligibility questions and possible elections before commissioning the study. Startup status or product development alone does not establish qualifying research or an available credit.

parts.title: Pull payroll and QRE data for the study
parts.guidance: Tie requested payroll, time allocations, contractor agreements, supply costs and technical records to the relevant business components and period. Distinguish documented activity from estimates needing explanation, and reconcile expenses to the books. Ask the people who performed or recorded the work to resolve gaps. Give the study team traceable activity and expense evidence for evaluating which costs qualify.

parts.title: Provider computes the credit and drafts Form 6765
parts.guidance: Reconcile the technical study, qualified-expense analysis and credit calculation for the filing year. Ask the provider to explain exclusions, the chosen method, group issues and proposed elections. Check draft Form 6765 and schedules against that analysis and the books. Resolve unsupported assumptions or inconsistent amounts before the claim enters the return-review process.

parts.title: Review the study and credit amount
parts.guidance: Verify the study’s technical descriptions, expense allocations and exclusions with the people who know the work and records. Review the method, substantiation and proposed elections with the tax adviser, including any payroll-credit treatment. Resolve discrepancies and retain the reviewed calculation with its supporting evidence before the claim is authorized through the company’s tax-filing process.

parts.title: File Form 6765 with the federal return
parts.guidance: Reconcile Form 6765 and required schedules with the supporting calculations, research records and filing-year instructions. If the company is making an eligible payroll-credit election, make it on a timely original income-tax return. Resolve the intended treatment before submission and complete the signature and filing requirements for that entity’s return. Preserve the filed form and acceptance evidence so the later payroll application uses the election amount and actual filing date.

parts.title: Elect the payroll offset and apply it in payroll
parts.guidance: Apply the election using the filed Form 6765, election amount, income-tax filing date and EIN. Calculate the usable credit on Form 8974 and attach it to the applicable employment-tax return. For Form 941 filers, start with the first quarter beginning after the income-tax return was filed; Form 943 and 944 filers follow the annual instructions. Use the company’s existing filing process and reconcile the credit used and remaining carryforward.

verify.how: Form 8974 carries the elected credit onto the payroll returns and the provider shows it offsetting employer payroll tax on subsequent runs.

metadata.supportReason: The QRE data pulls from payroll and accounting are automatable and a study provider drives Form 6765; the eligibility judgment, study review, and the return filing itself stay human.

geoNotes.summary: No US-style credit since the 200% weighted deduction lapsed: R&D spend now deducts at 100%, and DSIR recognition of an in-house R&D unit is the gateway to the remaining incentives (customs/GST concessions, government R&D schemes).
The UK analog is R&D tax relief claimed on the CT600 — a merged SME/RDEC scheme for accounting periods from April 2024, with a mandatory additional-information form before the claim.

The Forschungszulage (research allowance) refunds 25% of qualifying R&D wages — more for SMEs since 2024 — claimed in two steps: a project certificate from the BSFZ, then the allowance claim with the tax return via ELSTER.
France's CIR refunds 30% of qualifying R&D spend (with the CII for innovation on top), claimed with the corporate tax return — one of the most generous schemes in Europe.
The analog is SIFIDE II: a corporate-tax credit for R&D expenditure claimed with the Modelo 22, with the qualifying R&D certified by ANI (Agência Nacional de Inovação) on an annual application.

SR&ED is the closest thing anywhere to the US research credit — CCPCs earn an enhanced refundable credit on qualified R&D salaries and materials, claimed with the T2 on prescribed forms and defended with project records.
